belief: “I don’t hurt anybody else, so this is my choice and it is fine.”
belief_plain: I don’t hurt anybody else, so this is my choice and it is fine
origins: “I don’t hurt anybody else, so this is my choice and it is fine” can come from a real desire not to be a burden, or from a wish to keep this private. Sometimes it is also a way to end the conversation. You do not need a list of people you have harmed in order to be worth helping. Your own life matters. And lives are connected: the people who love you are affected even when you are careful, even when you cannot see it, even when you are trying not to hurt them. This is not a speech to make you feel like a destroyer. It is an invitation to let your life count, including to you. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure.
self: It is my body and my business.
If they do not know, it does not count.
I am not hurting them, so I should be left alone.
Getting help would worry people, so hiding is kinder.
I do not matter enough for this to be a problem.
replacement: My life matters, to God and to people who love me. I can get help because I am worth caring for.
